text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Ministers threaten to oppose extra 1.8 billion shekel cut in 1997 budget.
- Minister Sharansky opposes legislation invalidating conversions to Judaism performed outside Israel by any but Orthodox stream but opposes allowing conversions by any but Orthodox in Israel.
- U.S. Jerusalem Consul General Abington hopes document drafted with U.S. help on Hebron will lead to summit.
- Histadrut to call nationwide strike in two weeks unless budget cuts modified so as not to hit child subsidies, education, housing, and social security allocations to pensioners among other things.
- Government to float 10 percent stake in Bank Leumi in May.
- Haifa's Elscint signs agreement with Siemens to jointly develop and produce electromedical technology.
HAARETZ
- Estimate: Government will approve additional cut in budget despite opposition of education and foreign ministers.
- Time Magazine: The Palestinians are trying to get anti- tank missiles and missiles against planes.
- Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon say they will no longer honour understandings reached after Israel's April blitz.
- Head of manpower in army says religiously observant officers will remain minority as long as majority of population is secular.
- Senior member of Bar Association to meet today with justice minister and High Court president.
- Israel to raise $200 million in 1997 on Japanese bond market.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Today the Battle of the Budget.
- Palestinian President Arafat is accumulating antitank missiles, Time Magazine says.
- Rate of inflation in Israel is lower than official rate by 0.7 percent annually, government statistician says.
- Consumer Council wants rise in Cellcom rates put off.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu says budget cuts involve victims but the burden will be evenly spread.
- Iran has "air train" bringing weapons to Lebanon's Hizbollah guerrillas via Syria, says senior source.
GLOBES
- Finance Minister Meridor: Without a meaningful budget cut now, it will be hard to win the next elections.
